result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers choose the button spinner for the right reasons: the 1–6 second wait has no known length, and the payment must not go through twice. Both also explain clearly why the fixed progress bar and the modal don't fit. B wins narrowly because its success moment is more precise: it gives exact timings and easing, a delayed spinner so fast charges don't flash, a persistent confirmation message, highlighting only the person's own gift, and reduced-motion handling. A handles long waits better, with a hard timeout that tells the person whether the card was charged. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers pick option A and tie it to the 1–6 second wait and the double-charge risk. Both also explain clearly why the fixed 3-second bar and the heavy modal are a poor fit. Answer A is more exact about the success animation, with timings and easing for each step. Answer B is better on the slow and failed cases: it adds a hard timeout that tells the person whether the card was charged, warns them not to refresh, and keeps the 'Give $25' button from reappearing and inviting an accidental second gift.
